response.assayComponentEndpointDesc: Data from the assay component TOX21_ARE_KS_LUC_Agonist was analyzed into 2 assay endpoints. This assay endpoint, TOX21_ARE_KS_LUC_Agonist was analyzed in the positive analysis fitting direction relative to DMSO as the negative control and baseline of activity. Using a type of inducible reporter, gain-of-signal activity can be used to understand changes in binding. To generalize the intended target to other relatable targets, this assay endpoint is annotated to the nuclear receptor, where the subfamily is non-steroidal.
response.assayComponentDesc: TOX21_ARE_KS_LUC_Agonist is one of two assay component(s) measured or calculated from the TOX21_ARE_KS_LUC_Agonist assay. It is designed to make measurements of luciferase induction, a form of inducible reporter, as detected with bioluminescence signals by CellTiter-Glo Luciferase-coupled ATP quantitation technology.
response.assayComponentTargetDesc: The antioxidant response element (ARE) signaling pathway plays an important role in the amelioration of oxidative stress. The activation of the ARE report gene can be detected by ONE-Glo Luciferase Assay System to identify agonists that induce oxidative stress.
response.assayDesc: TOX21_ARE_KS_LUC_Agonist is a cell-based, single-readout assay that uses HaCAT, a human skin cell line, with measurements taken at 24 hours after chemical dosing in a 1536-well plate. See tox21-ks-are-p1.
response.assaySourceLongName: Toxicology in the 21st Century federal research collaboration
response.assaySourceDesc: The Toxicology in the 21st Century (Tox21) program aims to develop better toxicity assessment methods to quickly and efficiently test whether certain chemical compounds have the potential to disrupt processes in the human body that may lead to negative health effects. The Tox21 consortium is a federal collaboration between EPA, the National Toxicology Program (NTP) headquartered at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The NIH Chemical Genomics Center (NCGC) is the primary screening facility running ultra high-throughput screening assays across a large interagency-developed chemical library, often referred to as the Tox21 10K Library.
